Landing and the front bedroom squeak like mad, especially the board right outside the bathroom door, which wakes Lucía every time I get up at 5:45 for work. Lifted the carpet on 15 Feb 2025. Boards are original 1930s pine, tongue and groove, 140mm wide, nailed with cut nails into 4x2 joists at about 400mm centres. Found the culprits by walking on them and marking with chalk: 6 noisy spots. Before any screw went in I lifted one board near the airing cupboard to check where cables and pipes run (the upstairs ring runs across the landing about 50mm under the boards, and the 15mm heating pipes run along the joists). Marked the safe zones on the board tops in pencil. Fix was 50mm Spax flooring screws, 2 per joist, countersunk, about 15mm away from the old nail, pilot drilled 3mm so the old pine didn't split. Talc brushed into the gaps where boards rub each other. Went from 6 to 1 noise, the last one is between joists where a bit of noggin is needed, job for when the carpet comes up again. Box of 200 screws £14.20 from Toolstation, used 34.
